To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NTHi establishes a niche in the COPD airway by expressing multiple redundant adhesions that mediate binding, evading host immune recognition and forming biofilms.

NTHi has adapted to the hostile environment of COPD airways by expressing multiple redundant adhesions that mediate attachment to host cellular and ECM components and by evading host immune clearance by invading host airway epithelial cells, binding host serum proteins, forming biofilm and displaying antigenic variation.

NTHi has developed multiple mechanisms of persistence that facilitate infection of the COPDs airways, and that these mechanisms contribute to chronic airway inflammatory responses and the progressive loss of lung function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how NTHi causes disease, which may ultimately lead to the identification of novel targets for the development of therapeutics that can prevent and/or treat NTHi infections.
understanding the mechanisms that contribute to the persistence of bacterial pathogens in the airways of patients with COPD.
the role of bacterial pathogens in the pathophysiology of chronic airway diseases, and the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of these conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

NTHi infection is a significant contributor to the burden of COPDs and that the mechanisms that allow NTHi persistence in the COPD airway are a major factor contributing to the chronicity of the disease.
NTHi has developed multiple strategies to evade host immune responses and establish infection in the COPD airway.
persistent NTHi infection in the COPD airway is a significant contributor to the morbidity and mortality associated with the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

NTHi is a highly successful pathogen that is well adapted to the hostile environment of COPD airways and has evolved multiple mechanisms that allow it to persist for prolonged periods of time, causing chronic airway inflammation and progressive loss of pulmonary functions.
NTHi is a highly adaptable pathogen that has developed multiple mechanisms to evade host defenses and to establish a niche within the hostile COPD lung.
NTHi has developed multiple mechanisms to evade the immune response and establish persistent infection in the airways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the persistent infection of the airways by NTHi contributes to chronic airways inflammation and the accelerated loss of pulmonary function that is a hallmark of COPD.

persistent NTHi airway infection in COPD is a dynamic process involving multiple mechanisms that allow the pathogenic bacteria to evade host immune clearance, and to establish a persistent infection in the airways.
